title: Jerusalem! My Glorious Home
description: Jerusalem! My Glorious Home in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 558 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Society of Heaven”, where the book credits them to the Christian Psalmist.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-ru-sa-lem! my glo-rious home! Name ev-er dear to me! When shall my la-bors have an end In joy, and peace and thee? When shall these eyes thy heaven built walls And pear-ly gates be-hold? Thy bul-warks with sal-va-tion strong, And streets of shin-ing gold.

lines: When shall my labors have an end
In joy, and peace and thee?
When shall these eyes thy heaven-built walls
There happier bowers than Eden's bloom,
Blest seats! through rude and stormy scenes
Why should I shrink at pain and woe?
I've Canaan's goodly land in view,
And soon my friends in Christ below
My soul still pants for thee;
Then shall my labors have an end,
When I thy joys shall see.

credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
